 ii) To hold and declare the entire acquisition  proceeding bearing Case No.14/84-85 as instituted by  the respondent State in relation to the properties of the  petitioners concern to have been lapsed also in light of Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 as no  award has been made uptil now since passing of the  notification of publication in the year 1985 and  declaration in the year 1987.

iii) To hold and declare that in light of Section  17(3-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, taking of the  possession of the property of the petitioners without  tendering payment of 80 percentum of the  compensation is illegal and therefore no possession in  the eyes of law.

iv) To issue an appropriate writ/order/direction  in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondent  authorities to provide the cost of acquisition as define  under Section 3(i) of the Right to Fair Compensation  and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation  and Resettlement Act,2013 as the respondent State has  already constructed the road on the acquired property  Patna High Court CWJC No.3051 of 2016 dt.13-08-2024  4/7  of the petitioners without making any award and  without payment of any compensation thereafter.
 v) To issue an appropriate writ/order/direction  in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondent  authorities to pass an award under the new Act on the  basis of the current market value of the lands in  question in light of the provisions of the Right to Fair  Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
 Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,2013 and  compensate the petitioners accordingly.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in the  year 1968, the State took a decision for construction of road  from Begusarai to Birpur Sanjat in the district of Begusarai and,
 accordingly, Gazette notification for acquisition of land for the  aforesaid purpose was made vide Notification No. 285 dated  10.05.1985 .
Thereafter, in view of the aforesaid notification, the lands of the petitioners were acquired.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that though under the provisions of the Act, 1894 specially Section 11-A, the award was to be made Patna High Court CWJC No.3051 of 2016 dt.13-08-2024 within a period of two years from the date of publication of declaration but, till date,
i.e. even after lapse of approximately 47 years, neither any award has been made nor any compensation paid to the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners then submits that the present case is entirely covered by the orders both dated 09.01.2024 passed by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in C.W.J.C. Nos. 7705 of 2016 and 7717 of 2016 respectively and the present case may also be disposed of in the same terms.
5. A counter-affidavit has been filed in this case on behalf of the Respondent Nos. 3 to 6.

Paragraph Nos. 5, 6 & 8 of the said counter-affidavit, being relevant, read as follows:-
"5) That in this connection it is important to mention here that a land acquisition proceeding 79/66- 67 was started by the respondents for the acquisition of the land of petitioners and declaration was published but due to some mistake in the said declaration, this land acquisition officer sent a letter no.-806 dated 24.09.1989 to the under secretary of Revenue and land Reforms department, Patna,
for its correction, but the same was not corrected and in the mean time the said scheme lapsed due to coming in force of new Land Acquisition Amendment Act, 1984.
That after several letters were sent by D.L.A.O., Begusarai to the requisitioning department there is no fresh requisition sent by the same up till now.
Therefore the payment of compensation could not be made.

Patna High Court CWJC No.3051 of 2016 dt.13-08-2024 6) That at present the respondents have taken steps for acquiring the Land under provision of law,
and the D.M. Begusarai has sent a letter no.124 dated 10.03.16 to the Principal Secretary, Road Construction Department, Patna for direction to the Executive Engineer, Road Construction department, Begusarai, to send fresh requisition.
Hence this writ application is not maintainable and fit to be dismissed.

4 8) That the petitioners have themselves admitted that so many writ by different persons have been filed for the same reliefs and these writs are still pending before this Hon'ble Court, so in view of the above fact the petitioners are not entitled to any relief or reliefs as mentioned in sub para (i) to (Vii)
of this para.

Begusarai for sending fresh requisition for acquisition of the lands of the petitioners, so that compensation be paid to the petitioners at the earliest."
6.
